evidence.snippet: The benzimidazole anthelmintics, mebendazole and albendazole, are commonly used to remove these infections.
Adult worms feed on the blood of a host and can cause iron deficiency anaemia

evidence.reference_title: Trichuris trichiura infection in children: Two case reports and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Most children with whipworm disease as well as blood in the stool present with mild to moderate small-cell hypochromic anemia, while severe anemia can be observed in certain cases.

nodes.description: Ascaris lumbricoides worms can obstruct the intestinal lumen, producing intestinal obstruction. Most intestinal infections are asymptomatic.

evidence.snippet: Patients with A. lumbricoides infection warrant anthelminthic treatment, even if they are asymptomatic, to prevent complications from migration of the parasite.
The majority of patients with intestinal ascariasis are asymptomatic.
Hyperinfection is characterized by exponential increase in parasitic burden, leading to tissue invasion and life-threatening disease and associated bloodstream infections due to enteric organisms.

nodes.description: Mucosal injury produces low-grade continuous bleeding into the gut lumen. Each adult worm accounts for roughly 0.005 mL of blood per day, so worm burden and duration of infection determine the cumulative loss.

evidence.reference_title: Trichuris trichiura infection in children: Two case reports and literature review.
evidence.snippet: the amount of bleeding caused by each adult parasite is 0.005 mL/d

evidence.reference_title: The public health significance of Trichuris trichiura.
evidence.snippet: The blood loss that can occur in T. trichiura infection is likely to contribute to anaemia

nodes.description: The embedded worm inflicts mechanical damage and chemical stimulation on the colonic mucosa. The degree of that mucosal injury tracks the clinical course of the infection.
nodes.id: Colonic mucosal mechanical and chemical injury

evidence.reference_title: Trichuris trichiura infection in children: Two case reports and literature review.
evidence.snippet: The clinical symptoms and course of the disease, the number of parasites and the response to treatment are closely related to the degree of intestinal mucosal injury.

nodes.description: Systemic corticosteroids, and other causes of immune suppression such as solid-organ transplantation and HTLV-1 infection, convert a chronic subclinical Strongyloides stercoralis infection into hyperinfection.
nodes.id: Corticosteroid therapy in a Strongyloides-infected host

evidence.snippet: The use of corticosteroids and HTLV-1 infection are most commonly associated with the hyperinfection syndrome.
Autoinfection, in which larvae generated in the host go on to re-infect the host, leads to a state of chronic asymptomatic infection often with eosinophilia.

Complications include Löeffler syndrome, intestinal obstruction, biliary colic, recurrent pyogenic cholangitis, cholecystitis, acalculous cholecystitis, obstructive jaundice, cholelithiasis, pancreatitis, and malnutrition.

evidence.reference_title: Parasitic-induced Loeffler's syndrome: A systematic review based on clinical reports.
evidence.snippet: Loeffler's syndrome, an uncommon pulmonary disorder characterized by transient lung infiltrates and peripheral eosinophilia, is often misdiagnosed as pneumonia. Commonly associated with parasitic infections such as Ascaris lumbricoides and Strongyloides stercoralis

evidence.reference_title: The public health significance of Trichuris trichiura.
evidence.snippet: The Trichuris dysentery syndrome (TDS) associated with heavy T. trichiura, which includes chronic dysentery, rectal prolapse, anaemia, poor growth, and clubbing of the fingers constitutes an important public health problem

Complications include Löeffler syndrome, intestinal obstruction, biliary colic, recurrent pyogenic cholangitis, cholecystitis, acalculous cholecystitis, obstructive jaundice, cholelithiasis, pancreatitis, and malnutrition.

nodes.description: Ivermectin is the treatment for Strongyloides stercoralis infection, and people from endemic areas who are about to start immune-suppressive therapy should be screened and treated beforehand to prevent hyperinfection.

evidence.snippet: Ivermectin is highly effective in treating the disease.

nodes.description: Larvae of Ascaris, hookworms and Strongyloides pass through the lungs during their migration to the intestine. The transit draws eosinophils into the airways and lung parenchyma, usually without permanent lung damage.
nodes.id: Nematode larval migration through the lungs

evidence.snippet: Most of the nematodes multiply within the human host and cause pulmonary eosinophilia during larval migration through the lungs.
In the Western world, the most common infections are caused by Strongyloides, Ascaris, Toxocara, and Ancylostoma species.

nodes.description: Unlike the other soil-transmitted helminths, Strongyloides stercoralis larvae generated inside the host can re-infect the same host. This autoinfection sustains a chronic, often asymptomatic infection that can persist for decades, frequently with eosinophilia.

evidence.snippet: Autoinfection, in which larvae generated in the host go on to re-infect the host, leads to a state of chronic asymptomatic infection often with eosinophilia.

nodes.description: In an immunosuppressed host the parasite burden rises exponentially and larvae invade tissues beyond the intestine, carrying enteric bacteria into the bloodstream. Hyperinfection is life-threatening.

evidence.snippet: Hyperinfection is characterized by exponential increase in parasitic burden, leading to tissue invasion and life-threatening disease and associated bloodstream infections due to enteric organisms.

nodes.description: Adult Trichuris trichiura burrow their slender anterior end into the epithelium of the cecum and colon, anchoring the worm in the mucosa. This is the initiating event of the whipworm arm, distinct from hookworm's direct blood-feeding mechanism.
nodes.id: Trichuris anterior-end embedding in colonic mucosa

evidence.reference_title: Trichuris trichiura infection in children: Two case reports and literature review.
evidence.snippet: The front end of the parasites burrows into the intestinal epithelium, feeds on blood and tissue fluid, and causes disease through mechanical damage, chemical stimulation and nutrient plundering in the host intestine.
